History:
- Presenting complaint: Acute shortness of breath starting about 1 hour ago at rest; cough began yesterday.
- Onset/duration/progression: SOB started within the last hour; currently not clearly worsening; coughing since yesterday.
- Context: Watching TV when SOB began; recent cesarean section 4 weeks ago; patient is with baby.
- Associated symptoms: Chest soreness on deep inspiration; no chest pain reported.
- Respiratory/infectious history: No productive cough (no sputum produced reported); prior flu-like illness not recent; no other medical problems noted.
- Peripartum status: Post-Cesarean 4 weeks ago; on pain medications post-delivery (Codeine) but not currently taking.
- Triggers/stress: Patient reports feeling stressed and heart racing sensation.
- Allergies: Allergic to Ibuprofen.

Past Medical History:
- Recent cesarean section: 4 weeks ago.
- Allergies: Ibuprofen.
- Medications: Codeine analgesia after C-section; had been taking it regularly but not for about a week; currently not taking Codeine.

Physical Examination:
- Symptoms observed/reported: Shortness of breath at rest; chest soreness on deep breath; C-section scar tender.
- Cardiovascular: Patient reports heart racing; clinician noted heart rate running slightly fast based on counting.
- Respiratory: Cough nonproductive; no chest pain reported.
- Other: Baby present; no other medical problems described.

Impression:
- Acute shortness of breath in the postpartum patient with recent cesarean section; concern for postoperative venous thromboembolism (DVT/PE) requiring hospital evaluation.

Management Plan:
- Immediate action: Advise urgent hospital evaluation for possible venous thromboembolism.
- Transportation: Self-transport to hospital with the baby (ambulance also an option; patient chose self-transport).
- Medications: Do not take Codeine for the time being.
- Safety/education: Explain clot risk after cesarean section; if hospital confirms a clot, treatment may be provided.
- Additional guidance: Bring baby and essential items to hospital.

Patient Summary:
- A postpartum woman (4 weeks after cesarean) developed acute shortness of breath with a recent cough and chest soreness. There is concern for possible blood clots (DVT/PE) related to recent surgery. She chose to go to the hospital with her baby for evaluation and was advised to avoid Codeine until seen.

Key Takeaways:
- Seek urgent hospital assessment to evaluate for venous thromboembolism after recent cesarean section.
- Do not take Codeine until cleared by healthcare providers.
- Bring the baby and essential items if going to the hospital; hospital evaluation will determine next steps.

Next Steps:
- Hospital evaluation to assess for clots (DVT/PE) and related workup; management or treatment to be determined by hospital team.

Quality checks:
- Missing elements clinically expected for a consult:
  - Vital signs documented (no formal vitals provided; clinician only noted “heart running slightly fast” without a measured value).
  - Full medication reconciliation and current medication list beyond Codeine; no chronic meds detailed.
  - Complete past medical history beyond the C-section and Ibuprofen allergy (no chronic illnesses or prior hospitalizations documented).
  - No imaging or laboratory results available in transcript.
- Internal conflicts:
  - Conflict noted in DOB: patient stated date of birth as 20 April 1980s; clinician stated 1983.
- Transcript quality:
  - Conversation includes repetitions and incomplete phrases; some details (exact vitals, comprehensive ROS) are not documented. Overall content is oriented toward risk assessment and urgent referral.
